name: DX Hunter
description: DX Hunter is designed to make HF band operation faster and more organized. When you find activity on a frequency, mark it instantly, continue scanning the band, and jump back to your stored frequencies whenever you want — without having to remember or write them down.

features.title: Mark frequencies instantly
features.description: Found an active or interesting frequency? Mark it immediately and continue searching the band. No need to write frequencies down or try to remember them.

features.title: Navigate between marked frequencies
features.description: Move quickly backward and forward with < TO DO and TO DO >, or use the mouse wheel over marking and navigation buttons. Navigation visits pending TO DO frequencies and restores the saved operating mode, including frequencies with previous completed QSOs.

features.title: TO DO / TO SKIP / QSO DONE
features.description: Green QSO DONE bars stay above the graph's center line. Yellow TO DO and red TO SKIP bars appear below it at the exact frequency position. Completed and pending markers can coexist. Press TO DO to prepare another contact at a completed frequency; UNMARK preserves logged contacts.

features.title: ADIF export
features.description: Generate an ADIF log file from your completed QSOs for easy import into QRZ.com and other logging software that supports the ADIF standard.

features.title: Cabrillo export for contests
features.description: Export completed contacts with sent and received exchanges. A contest name is required; check the exported format against your contest rules.

features.title: Direct DSP control
features.description: Adjust DNR, SHIFT and WIDTH directly from the computer interface while operating, without navigating through radio menus.

features.title: Multiple QSOs on one frequency
features.description: Log different stations on the same frequency without overwriting previous contacts. Press TO DO to prepare the next contact. The graph shows all worked callsigns in green and the pending callsign in yellow.

features.title: Live contest duplicate warnings
features.description: In Contest Mode, a possible duplicate warning appears while typing a callsign already worked on the same band in the current contest. You can still confirm the contact when contest rules permit it. Checks do not save or refresh the log on every keystroke.

features.title: Configurable contest exchanges
features.description: Record sent and received exchanges. Configure a fixed exchange, automatic serial numbering, or a combination such as {serial} SC . Contest mode requires a callsign, both RSTs and both exchanges before confirming a contact. Outside contest mode, exchange fields and labels are disabled and serial numbers are not incremented. DATA settings apply when leaving the tab.

features.title: Confirmed contacts at a glance
features.description: The QSO tab lists every contact independently, including multiple contacts on the same frequency. Review UTC date/time, callsign, exact frequency, mode, RSTs, exchanges and comments. Sort columns or delete one selected QSO without removing other contacts at that frequency.

features.title: Automatic QSO recovery
features.description: All completed contacts, frequency markers, pending contact details and the next serial number are recovered on startup. Existing recovery files migrate automatically to version 1.0.1's format. No log export is required before closing.

features.title: Connect your way
features.description: CONNECT/DISCONNECT is in the SERIAL tab. Enable “Connect automatically on startup” to connect with your saved settings. The display shows DISCONNECTED while disconnected. The radio connection closes automatically when you exit.

features.title: Quick signal reports
features.description: Set sent and received RSTs to 59 with separate buttons beside each field. A callsign and both reports are required for every confirmed QSO; contest mode also requires both exchanges.

features.title: Smoother keyboard entry
features.description: TAB and Shift+TAB skip action buttons, and the read-only QSO date/time field does not receive focus. Edits are applied when a field loses focus, including when switching tabs, except where an explicit SAVE button is provided. CALLSIGN, COMMENTS, MY CALLSIGN and both exchange fields use uppercase text. Tab titles also stay out of the keyboard focus sequence. Editable contact fields have a lighter background so they are easy to identify.

features.title: Contact comments
features.description: Add notes about a station or contact using the COMMENTS field beside CALLSIGN.

features.title: Version and project information
features.description: The ABOUT tab shows DX Hunter 1.0.1, the author and clickable yellow links to email, the website, GitHub and releases.

features.title: Local and UTC clocks
features.description: Live clocks above the control panel show the PC's local time above UTC, with both updated every second.

features.title: VFO A frequency
features.description: Monitor the current VFO A frequency in real time and change frequency directly from DX Hunter.

features.title: Operating modes
features.description: Select LSB, USB, CW, FM and AM directly from the interface.

features.title: DNR, SHIFT and WIDTH
features.description: Frequently adjusted DSP controls remain immediately accessible while you operate and move between stations.

steps: Find activity Tune normally across the band using your FTDX10.
Press TO DO Store the current frequency and operating mode immediately and continue searching.
Keep exploring Mark as many interesting frequencies as you find.
Jump between them Use the navigation controls to move quickly through the stored frequencies.
Complete the QSO Enter the callsign and both RST reports, then press QSO DONE. Other marked frequencies remain available for QSOs still to be made.
installation: Download the ZIP and extract dx-hunter.exe into a writable folder.

When upgrading to 1.0.1, back up your QSO recovery JSON file and keep all settings and recovery files beside the new executable. Previous recovery files migrate automatically; the updated format requires version 1.0.1 or later.
Connect your FTDX10 by USB, with its USB serial driver installed.
Run dx-hunter.exe. In SERIAL, select your radio's CAT COM port and matching settings, then click CONNECT. Enable “Connect automatically on startup” if desired.

Use TO DO to store a station's frequency and mode, or TO SKIP to mark a station to skip. The navigation buttons and mouse wheel revisit only TO DO stations. Enter CALLSIGN, RST S and RST R before QSO DONE; the “59” buttons fill each report individually.
For contests, enable Contest mode in DATA and configure your exchange and optional serial number. Both sent and received exchanges are then required. Settings apply when you leave DATA.
Review confirmed contacts in QSO and export ADIF or Cabrillo as needed.
To work another station on a frequency with completed QSOs, press TO DO. Existing contacts and their green marker remain in the log; complete the new contact with QSO DONE.
